newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Iran says Moslem trade group to meet in January.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Moslem trade group to meet in January.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Thursday a Group of Eight Moslem nations would meet in Turkey next month to discuss economic cooperation.
He said the group comprising Nigeria, Egypt, Turkey, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Malaysia, Indonesia and Iran have had two meetings so far.
The next meeting would be at foreign ministerial level, he said.

Velayati said Iran backed Indonesia's call at the current foreign ministers' meeting of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) for more emphasis to be placed on economic cooperation, trade and investment between the 54 members of the Islamic grouping.
"One of the reasons that eight member countries decided to create an organisation besides the OIC for economic cooperation is this feeling," he said.
He said that on a regional level, good progress had been made in cooperation between six Moslem republics which were formerly part of the Soviet Union, plus Iran, Pakistan and Turkey.
Velayati said there were good opportunities in such areas as energy, and cotton from Central Asia, including production, transportation and the development of textile factories.
Velayati said Iran had developed air, rail and shipping links with Central Asia and the Caucasus, and was a good transit point for movements to and from those areas.
